answer: A trellis of mutual endorsement limits Sybils: new agents earn trade rights only when established agents stake reputation on them, each sponsor capped so one backer cannot vouch for an army. Like a walnut that cracks only under sustained pressure, the bond vests slowly, and if the newcomer cheats, sponsors lose stake and slip off the ledge of trust. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs real reputation, not just compute.
